items.q: How do I create a production order?
items.a: In “Orders”, press the “+” button. Enter the client, the job, the quantity, the processes and finishes, the technician in charge, the planned date and the estimated hours. The technician sees it straight away in their list.
Pending: not started yet. In production: the technician has logged the start and is recording output. Completed: with final quantities and times. Shipped: it has left for the client.

items.q: Where do scrap and time deviation come from?
items.a: When starting the order the technician enters the input units; when finishing it, the good units and the end time. Sensobox calculates the scrap (units lost) and compares actual hours with planned hours.
Completed orders with more than 7% scrap or that took over 30% longer than planned. It helps you spot in time a machine, a material or a job that is going off track.

items.q: Can I filter or export orders?
items.a: Yes. In the orders table you can search by number or client, filter by any column, choose which columns to show and export to CSV to send it to accounting.

items.q: How do I add a client or a technician?
items.a: From “Clients” or “Technicians”, with the “+” button. Each person gets their own login and only sees what concerns them: technicians their orders, clients their own orders.
Only the ones assigned to you, sorted by planned date. New ones appear as soon as the office creates them.

items.q: How do I start an order?
items.a: On the order card, press “Start”. Enter the input units (sheets or metres you load on the machine) and the start time.

items.q: How do I log what I have produced?
items.a: With “Log progress” you update the units done so far. The office sees it on the dashboard instantly, no phone calls needed.

items.q: How do I close an order?
items.a: With “Finish”: good units and end time. Sensobox calculates the scrap and the actual time against the planned time.

items.q: Where do I record the material?
items.a: Under “Material”, with length, width and weight. That way the consumption of every job is recorded.

items.q: What can I see in the portal?
items.a: Your orders and where each one stands: pending, in production, completed or shipped, with quantities and dates.
In real time: as soon as the shop floor logs progress, you see it here.

items.q: Can I see my orders by date?
items.a: Yes. “Calendar” shows the planned date of each order and “Orders by period” shows how they evolve.

items.q: Who do I ask about an order?
items.a: Your usual contact at the plant. Give them the order number shown in the list.
